entries.overview: A soft, fist-sized purplish organ tucked high under the left lower ribcage just beside the stomach.
entries.function: Filters worn-out red blood cells from the bloodstream and mounts fast immune responses against blood-borne microbes.

facts: White pulp pockets monitor the blood for pathogens while red pulp recycles iron and old red blood cells.
Acts as an emergency reserve holding extra platelets and immune monocytes.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Secondary Lymphoid Organs

entries.overview: One of two soft lobes of a flat lymphoid gland resting right behind the upper breastbone in front of the great vessels.
entries.function: Provides the specialized training site where immature T lymphocytes mature so they recognize threats safely.

facts: Reaches its largest size during childhood and gradually shrinks and fills with fat after puberty.
Trains T cells to attack foreign invaders without attacking the body’s own healthy tissues.
